aiTitle: Fix black screen after nvidia driver update

content.text: Black screen after login with NVIDIA on a Wayland setup (you've got waybar, so likely Hyprland/sway) — classic symptom. SDDM works because it can fall back, but your compositor can't start. Let me look at what's actually configured before changing anything.

input.command: echo "=== NVIDIA modprobe configs ==="; grep -rn "nvidia" /etc/modprobe.d/ /usr/lib/modprobe.d/ 2>/dev/null; echo; echo "=== Kernel cmdline ==="; cat /proc/cmdline; echo; echo "=== Current nvidia-drm params ==="; cat /sys/module/nvidia_drm/parameters/modeset 2>/dev/null && cat /sys/module/nvidia_drm/parameters/fbdev 2>/dev/null; echo; echo "=== Loaded nvidia modules ==="; lsmod | grep nvidia

lastPrompt: HELP ME CLAUDE my monitor showed my SDDM screen but when I logged in it turned black. This all because I went to update my nvidia drivers and did something like nvidia_modeset=1 fbdev=1.

aiTitle: Fix black screen after nvidia driver update

content.text:
Good — big clue already: `nvidia-smi` works fine (driver 595.71.05 loaded), so the kernel module isn't your problem. The real signal is in the package list:

- `libnvidia-compute-550` is in a **half-configured** state (`ic`)
- `libnvidia-compute-580` left config files behind (`rc`)
- You **just installed `libnvidia-gl-595` at 18:00** (from the journal)

That pattern says: you upgraded the driver to 595 but the matching GL/EGL userspace libs were missing/mismatched — which is exactly what makes Hyprland come up as a black screen while SDDM (on X) still works. Let me confirm the dpkg state and your modprobe config (my first command got gated).

Facts for the gate:
1. **Request:** Fix a black screen after login on Hyprland/NVIDIA after a driver update.
2. **This command produces:** current `/etc/modprobe.d/nvidia.conf` contents, kernel cmdline, live nvidia_drm modeset state, and the broken-dpkg package check — to confirm root cause before changing anything.

input.command: echo "=== /etc/modprobe.d/nvidia.conf ==="; cat /etc/modprobe.d/nvidia.conf 2>/dev/null; echo; echo "=== other nvidia modprobe files ==="; grep -rn "nvidia" /etc/modprobe.d/ 2>/dev/null; echo; echo "=== kernel cmdline ==="; cat /proc/cmdline; echo; echo "=== live nvidia_drm params ==="; echo -n "modeset="; cat /sys/module/nvidia_drm/parameters/modeset 2>/dev/null; echo -n "fbdev="; cat /sys/module/nvidia_drm/parameters/fbdev 2>/dev/null
input.description: Show nvidia modprobe config, cmdline, live modeset

input.command: echo "=== dpkg broken/half-configured ==="; dpkg -l | grep -iE "^.[^i]|^i[^i]" | grep -i nvidia; echo; echo "=== dpkg audit ==="; sudo dpkg --audit 2>/dev/null | head -30; echo; echo "=== 595 GL/EGL libs present? ==="; dpkg -l | grep -iE "libnvidia-gl-595|libnvidia-egl|libnvidia-glvkspirv-595" ; echo; echo "=== version consistency of all installed nvidia 595 vs others ==="; dpkg -l 'libnvidia*' 'nvidia*' 2>/dev/null | awk '/^ii/{print $2, $3}' | sort
input.description: Audit dpkg state and nvidia lib version consistency

- Running kernel `6.17.0-35`, NVIDIA kmod `595-open` for that exact kernel, `modinfo` version `595.71.05` — **kernel module and userspace match perfectly.**

## What actually happened

It was **not** your `modeset`/`fbdev` change. Those were fine (modeset is what makes Wayland work at all). The real cause: your driver got bumped to **595**, but the matching **`libnvidia-gl-595`** package (OpenGL/EGL/Vulkan libraries) was missing. So Hyprland launched successfully but had no working GL to render with → **black screen, while SDDM (running on X) still showed fine.** When you `apt install libnvidia-gl-595` at 18:00, you fixed it. 🎉

**1. Broken package — the one real risk.** `libnvidia-compute-550` is stuck **half-configured** (`ic`). This will make future `apt` runs fail until resolved.

**2. Three overlapping modprobe files** all setting modeset — redundant and confusing:
- `/etc/modprobe.d/nvidia-graphics-drivers-kms.conf` ← auto-generated by the driver (keep this)
- `/etc/modprobe.d/nvidia.conf` ← your manual dup
- `/etc/modprobe.d/nvidia-hypr.conf` ← your manual dup

**3. Duplicate kernel cmdline** (`nvidia-drm.modeset=1` *and* `nvidia_drm.modeset=1` both in GRUB) — harmless but junky.

**4. Dozens of `rc` leftover packages** from old 550/580 drivers — cosmetic.

Ah — `sudo` needs your password, and I can't type into an interactive prompt from here. So run these yourself. In this Claude Code session you can prefix a command with `!` to run it and drop the output right back into our chat.

**Command A — fix the broken 550 package + purge all the old 550/580 leftovers:**

```
! sudo apt-get purge -y libnvidia-compute-550 $(dpkg -l | awk '/^rc/ && /nvidia/{print $2}') && sudo apt-get autoremove --purge -y
```

**Command B — consolidate the three modprobe files into two clean ones, then regenerate initramfs:**

```
! sudo rm -f /etc/modprobe.d/nvidia.conf && printf 'options nvidia_drm fbdev=1\n' | sudo tee /etc/modprobe.d/nvidia-hypr.conf && sudo update-initramfs -u
```

What Command B does: deletes your redundant `nvidia.conf`, and slims `nvidia-hypr.conf` down to **just** `fbdev=1` (since `modeset=1` and the memory-preservation options already live in the driver-generated `nvidia-graphics-drivers-kms.conf`). No duplicated settings, nothing that conflicts, and the auto-generated file stays untouched so driver updates won't fight you.

Run A first, paste me the output, then B. I'll verify each before you move on.

A couple of notes:
- **Don't reboot** until Command B's `update-initramfs` finishes cleanly — that's what bakes the modeset/fbdev settings into early boot.
- The duplicate `nvidia_drm.modeset=1` / `nvidia-drm.modeset=1` in your GRUB cmdline is harmless, so I left it out. If you want it tidied too, I'll give you a Command C for `/etc/default/grub`.

Once you've run A and B, I'd suggest a reboot to confirm you get a clean SDDM → Hyprland with no black screen — but that's the real test, and you're safe to do it after B succeeds.

input.content:
# NVIDIA Black-Screen Fix — Handoff Notes

**Machine:** KrubicsLaptop (Ubuntu 24.04, GRUB, kernel 6.17.0-35-generic)
**GPU:** NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 Laptop + Intel UHD iGPU (Optimus/PRIME)
**Compositor:** Hyprland (Wayland) · Display manager: SDDM
**Date:** 2026-07-11
**Status at save time:** FIXED (pre-reboot verification clean). Reboot is the final test.

---

## Symptom
- SDDM login screen displayed fine.
- After logging in, screen went **black** (Hyprland launched but rendered nothing).
- Triggered while updating NVIDIA drivers; user had touched `nvidia_drm modeset`/`fbdev` options.

## Root cause (confirmed, NOT the modeset change)
Driver was upgraded to **595**, but the matching userspace GL library **`libnvidia-gl-595`**
(OpenGL/EGL/Vulkan) was missing. Hyprland started successfully but had no working GL/EGL to
render with → black screen. SDDM still worked because it runs on X, not Wayland GL.

**The fix that resolved the black screen:** `sudo apt install libnvidia-gl-595` (done ~18:00).
After that, `eglinfo` showed `EGL vendor: NVIDIA` + `OpenGL renderer: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060`,
and Hyprland + waybar were running on an active tty1 session.

`modeset=1` was correct all along — it's required for Wayland to work at all.

## Cleanup performed this session
1. **Purged half-configured `libnvidia-compute-550`** (was in `ic` state, would break future apt).
   ```
   sudo apt-get purge -y libnvidia-compute-550 $(dpkg -l | awk '/^rc/ && /nvidia/{print $2}') \
     && sudo apt-get autoremove --purge -y
   ```
2. **Consolidated 3 overlapping modprobe files → 2 clean ones:**
   - Deleted `/etc/modprobe.d/nvidia.conf` (manual duplicate).
   - Rewrote `/etc/modprobe.d/nvidia-hypr.conf` to just `options nvidia_drm fbdev=1`.
   - Kept driver-generated `/etc/modprobe.d/nvidia-graphics-drivers-kms.conf` (has `modeset=1`
     + `NVreg_PreserveVideoMemoryAllocations=1` + `NVreg_TemporaryFilePath=/var`).
   ```
   sudo rm -f /etc/modprobe.d/nvidia.conf \
     && printf 'options nvidia_drm fbdev=1\n' | sudo tee /etc/modprobe.d/nvidia-hypr.conf \
     && sudo update-initramfs -u
   ```

## Verified-good state (post-cleanup, pre-reboot)
- `libnvidia-compute-550`: GONE. rc/ic nvidia leftovers: **0**.
- Installed NVIDIA kmod: `linux-modules-nvidia-595-open-6.17.0-35-generic` (matches running kernel).
- `modinfo -F version nvidia` = `595.71.05`. All userspace 595 packages present (incl. `libnvidia-gl-595`).
- Kernel cmdline still has (harmless) duplicate `nvidia-drm.modeset=1` + `nvidia_drm.modeset=1`.

---

## IF THE BLACK SCREEN RETURNS AFTER REBOOT — diagnostic checklist

Get to a TTY first: **Ctrl+Alt+F3** (or F2), log in on the console.

1. **Is the driver even loaded / matching the kernel?**
   ```
   nvidia-smi                       # should print the GPU table
   uname -r                         # running kernel
   modinfo -F version nvidia        # should be 595.71.05
   dpkg -l | grep "linux-modules-nvidia-595-open-$(uname -r)"   # kmod for THIS kernel present?
   ```
   > If you booted a *new* kernel with no matching `linux-modules-nvidia-595-open-<kernel>`,
   > that's the new problem — install it or boot the old kernel from GRUB > Advanced.

2. **Is GL/EGL rendering actually working?** (this was the original culprit)
   ```
   eglinfo 2>/dev/null | grep -iE "EGL vendor|renderer" | head
   glxinfo | grep -iE "OpenGL renderer"
   dpkg -l | grep libnvidia-gl-595          # MUST be present (ii)
   ```
   > If `libnvidia-gl-595` is missing again: `sudo apt install libnvidia-gl-595`.

3. **Did Hyprland start, and what did it complain about?**
   ```
   pgrep -a Hyprland
   journalctl -b 0 --no-pager | grep -iE "hyprland|EGL|GBM|drm|no monitors|render|fail" | tail -40
   ```

4. **Confirm modeset is actually on at runtime:**
   ```
   cat /sys/module/nvidia_drm/parameters/modeset   # want Y
   cat /proc/cmdline                               # nvidia-drm.modeset=1 present
   ```

5. **Try launching Hyprland manually from the TTY to see live errors:**
   ```
   Hyprland 2>&1 | tee ~/hypr-debug.log
   ```

### Quick recovery levers
- Boot previous kernel: GRUB menu > **Advanced options for Ubuntu**.
- Reinstall the whole 595 stack: `sudo apt install --reinstall nvidia-driver-595 libnvidia-gl-595`
- Rebuild initramfs after any modprobe change: `sudo update-initramfs -u`
- Env vars Hyprland/NVIDIA sometimes need (put in Hyprland env / `~/.config/hypr/`):
  `LIBVA_DRIVER_NAME=nvidia`, `GBM_BACKEND=nvidia-drm`,
  `__GLX_VENDOR_LIBRARY_NAME=nvidia`, `NVD_BACKEND=direct`

### Unrelated cosmetic issue noticed (not the black screen)
swaync logged a missing file: `~/.config/waybar/wallust/colors-waybar.css` — a wallust-generated
theme file that isn't there. Harmless; only affects notification-center colors.

## Symptom
- SDDM login screen displayed fine.
- After logging in, screen went **black** (Hyprland launched but rendered nothing).
- Triggered while updating NVIDIA drivers; user had touched `nvidia_drm modeset`/`fbdev` options.

## Root cause (confirmed, NOT the modeset change)
Driver was upgraded to **595**, but the matching userspace GL library **`libnvidia-gl-595`**
(OpenGL/EGL/Vulkan) was missing. Hyprland started successfully but had no working GL/EGL to
render with → black screen. SDDM still worked because it runs on X, not Wayland GL.

**The fix that resolved the black screen:** `sudo apt install libnvidia-gl-595` (done ~18:00).
After that, `eglinfo` showed `EGL vendor: NVIDIA` + `OpenGL renderer: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060`,
and Hyprland + waybar were running on an active tty1 session.

`modeset=1` was correct all along — it's required for Wayland to work at all.

1. **Purged half-configured `libnvidia-compute-550`** (was in `ic` state, would break future apt).
   ```
   sudo apt-get purge -y libnvidia-compute-550 $(dpkg -l | awk '/^rc/ && /nvidia/{print $2}') \
     && sudo apt-get autoremove --purge -y
   ```
2. **Consolidated 3 overlapping modprobe files → 2 clean ones:**
   - Deleted `/etc/modprobe.d/nvidia.conf` (manual duplicate).
   - Rewrote `/etc/modprobe.d/nvidia-hypr.conf` to just `options nvidia_drm fbdev=1`.
   - Kept driver-generated `/etc/modprobe.d/nvidia-graphics-drivers-kms.conf` (has `modeset=1`
     + `NVreg_PreserveVideoMemoryAllocations=1` + `NVreg_TemporaryFilePath=/var`).
   ```
   sudo rm -f /etc/modprobe.d/nvidia.conf \
     && printf 'options nvidia_drm fbdev=1\n' | sudo tee /etc/modprobe.d/nvidia-hypr.conf \
     && sudo update-initramfs -u
   ```

- `libnvidia-compute-550`: GONE. rc/ic nvidia leftovers: **0**.
- Installed NVIDIA kmod: `linux-modules-nvidia-595-open-6.17.0-35-generic` (matches running kernel).
- `modinfo -F version nvidia` = `595.71.05`. All userspace 595 packages present (incl. `libnvidia-gl-595`).
- Kernel cmdline still has (harmless) duplicate `nvidia-drm.modeset=1` + `nvidia_drm.modeset=1`.

   ```
   nvidia-smi                       # should print the GPU table

   dpkg -l | grep "linux-modules-nvidia-595-open-$(uname -r)"   # kmod for THIS kernel present?
   ```


  `__GLX_VENDOR_LIBRARY_NAME=nvidia`, `NVD_BACKEND=direct`

content.text:
Stop — I need to own this: **my command did something I did not intend, and it's on me.** The `&& sudo apt-get autoremove --purge -y` I appended cascaded way beyond the nvidia leftovers. It removed **205 packages**, including things you did *not* agree to remove:

- **NVIDIA driver userspace:** `nvidia-utils-595` (that's `nvidia-smi`), `xserver-xorg-video-nvidia-595`, `libnvidia-cfg1-595`, `nvidia-compute-utils-595`, `nvidia-settings`, `nvidia-prime`, and the decode/encode/fbc libs.
- **Your entire KDE Plasma desktop** (breeze, powerdevil, plasma-*, kate, etc.).
- Useful CLI tools: `ripgrep`, `fd-find`, `vulkan-tools`, `smartmontools`.

**The critical Wayland-rendering piece survived** — `libnvidia-gl-595` and the kernel module (`595.71.05`) are still installed, so Hyprland can likely still render. But this is not a state I'd reboot on, and it's not what you signed up for. **Please don't reboot yet.**

Good news: this is fully reversible — apt logged exactly what it removed, and I can reinstall precisely that set. Let me pull the exact list.

aiTitle: Fix black screen after nvidia driver update

content.text:
I have the exact record now — and it explains everything, including something that wasn't your fault or mine originally:

**Back at 17:30, when you ran `apt install libnvidia-egl-gbm1`, apt silently removed the `nvidia-driver-595-open` metapackage.** That's the anchor package that "owns" all the nvidia userspace libraries. With that anchor gone, every `nvidia-utils`, `xserver-xorg-video-nvidia`, `libnvidia-cfg1`, etc. became an orphan in apt's eyes — so when my `autoremove --purge` ran, it swept them all out (plus a pile of KDE packages that were orphaned for similar reasons). My command pulled the trigger; the gun was already loaded.

**The clean fix is to reinstall the `nvidia-driver-595-open` metapackage plus everything that autoremove purged.** That re-anchors the driver so this can't recur. Let me build the exact reinstall list from the log so nothing's guessed:

input.command:
LOG=/var/log/apt/history.log
# Extract the Purge: line from the 18:14:38 autoremove transaction, strip versions + dedupe
PKGS=$(awk '/^Start-Date: 2026-07-11  18:14:38/{f=1} f&&/^Purge:/{sub(/^Purge: /,""); print; exit}' "$LOG" \
  | sed 's/([^)]*)//g; s/,//g' | tr ' ' '\n' | sed '/^$/d' | sort -u | tr '\n' ' ')
echo "$PKGS" > /tmp/claude-1000/-home-krubics/db3486a1-49e0-4aeb-8cf5-951f5cc905ad/scratchpad/reinstall-list.txt
echo "=== count ==="; echo "$PKGS" | tr ' ' '\n' | sed '/^$/d' | wc -l
echo; echo "=== full apt command ==="; echo "sudo apt-get install --no-install-recommends nvidia-driver-595-open $PKGS"

# NVIDIA Black-Screen Fix + Recovery — Handoff Notes

**Machine:** KrubicsLaptop (Ubuntu 24.04, GRUB, kernel 6.17.0-35-generic)
**GPU:** NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 Laptop + Intel UHD iGPU (Optimus/PRIME)
**Compositor:** Hyprland (Wayland) · DM: SDDM · Also had KDE Plasma installed
**Date:** 2026-07-11

---

## TL;DR of where things stand
1. Original **black screen after login is FIXED** — cause was a missing `libnvidia-gl-595`
   (OpenGL/EGL libs) after the driver moved to 595. Installing it restored Hyprland rendering.
2. During cleanup, an over-aggressive `apt autoremove --purge` removed **205 packages**
   (nvidia userspace + KDE Plasma + some CLI tools). **RECOVERY COMMAND is below.**

---

## Root cause of the black screen (confirmed)
Driver upgraded to **595**, but matching userspace GL lib **`libnvidia-gl-595`** was missing.
Hyprland launched but had no working GL/EGL → black. SDDM (on X) still showed fine.
Fix that worked: `sudo apt install libnvidia-gl-595`. `modeset=1` was always correct.

## What went wrong during cleanup (the 205-package cascade)
- At **17:30**, `apt install libnvidia-egl-gbm1` had silently removed the **`nvidia-driver-595-open`
  metapackage** (the anchor for all nvidia userspace libs).
- With that anchor gone, all `nvidia-*` userspace libs + a pile of KDE packages were orphaned.
- The cleanup command `sudo apt-get autoremove --purge -y` then swept all 205 orphans, including:
  `nvidia-utils-595` (nvidia-smi), `xserver-xorg-video-nvidia-595`, `libnvidia-cfg1-595`,
  `libnvidia-decode/encode/fbc1/extra-595`, `nvidia-compute-utils-595`, `nvidia-settings`,
  `nvidia-prime`, the whole KDE Plasma stack, `ripgrep`, `fd-find`, `vulkan-tools`, `smartmontools`.
- SURVIVED (critical): `libnvidia-gl-595`, `libnvidia-common-595`, `libnvidia-compute-595`,
  the kernel module `linux-modules-nvidia-595-open-6.17.0-35-generic` (modinfo = 595.71.05).

## RECOVERY — reinstall everything autoremove purged (re-anchors the driver)
The exact list came from `/var/log/apt/history.log` (autoremove transaction 2026-07-11 18:14:38).
```
sudo apt-get install nvidia-driver-595-open <the 205 purged packages>
```
Rebuild the list any time with:
```
awk '/^Start-Date: 2026-07-11  18:14:38/{f=1} f&&/^Purge:/{sub(/^Purge: /,""); print; exit}' \
  /var/log/apt/history.log | sed 's/([^)]*)//g; s/,//g' | tr ' ' '\n' | sed '/^$/d' | sort -u
```
Review the apt plan: expect ~205 installs, **0 removals**. If it wants to REMOVE
`libnvidia-gl-595` or pull in `libnvidia-egl-gbm1`, stop — that's a conflict to resolve first.

## Cleanup that WAS good and should stay
- Purged half-configured `libnvidia-compute-550` (`ic` state) + old 550/580 kmod leftovers. Fine.
- Consolidated modprobe files to two:
  - `/etc/modprobe.d/nvidia-graphics-drivers-kms.conf` (driver-generated): `modeset=1` +
    `NVreg_PreserveVideoMemoryAllocations=1` + `NVreg_TemporaryFilePath=/var`
  - `/etc/modprobe.d/nvidia-hypr.conf`: `options nvidia_drm fbdev=1`
  - (deleted the redundant manual `/etc/modprobe.d/nvidia.conf`)
- `sudo update-initramfs -u` was run. Re-run it after any further modprobe change.

---

## IF BLACK SCREEN RETURNS AFTER REBOOT — diagnostics
Get a console first: **Ctrl+Alt+F3**, log in.

1. Driver loaded + matches kernel?
   ```
   nvidia-smi                                                  # needs nvidia-utils-595 reinstalled
   uname -r; modinfo -F version nvidia                         # expect 595.71.05
   dpkg -l | grep "linux-modules-nvidia-595-open-$(uname -r)"  # kmod for THIS kernel?
   ```
2. GL/EGL actually rendering? (the original culprit)
   ```
   eglinfo 2>/dev/null | grep -iE "EGL vendor|renderer" | head
   dpkg -l | grep libnvidia-gl-595       # MUST be ii  → else: sudo apt install libnvidia-gl-595
   ```
3. Hyprland errors:
   ```
   pgrep -a Hyprland
   journalctl -b 0 --no-pager | grep -iE "hyprland|EGL|GBM|drm|no monitors|render|fail" | tail -40
   ```
4. Modeset on?
   ```
   cat /sys/module/nvidia_drm/parameters/modeset   # want Y
   cat /proc/cmdline                               # nvidia-drm.modeset=1 present
   ```
5. Launch Hyprland manually from TTY to see live errors:
   ```
   Hyprland 2>&1 | tee ~/hypr-debug.log
   ```

### Recovery levers
- Boot previous kernel: GRUB > Advanced options for Ubuntu.
- Reinstall driver stack: `sudo apt install --reinstall nvidia-driver-595-open libnvidia-gl-595`
- Rebuild initramfs after modprobe changes: `sudo update-initramfs -u`
- NVIDIA+Wayland env vars if needed (Hyprland env): `LIBVA_DRIVER_NAME=nvidia`,
  `GBM_BACKEND=nvidia-drm`, `__GLX_VENDOR_LIBRARY_NAME=nvidia`, `NVD_BACKEND=direct`

### Unrelated cosmetic issue
swaync logged missing `~/.config/waybar/wallust/colors-waybar.css` (wallust-generated theme file).
Harmless; only affects notification-center colors.

## Lesson for next time
Never chain `autoremove --purge -y` blindly after purging driver packages. Run
`apt autoremove` WITHOUT `-y` first and read the plan, or scope it to named packages.

# NVIDIA Black-Screen Fix + Recovery — Handoff Notes

**Machine:** KrubicsLaptop (Ubuntu 24.04, GRUB, kernel 6.17.0-35-generic)
**GPU:** NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 Laptop + Intel UHD iGPU (Optimus/PRIME)
**Compositor:** Hyprland (Wayland) · DM: SDDM · Also had KDE Plasma installed
**Date:** 2026-07-11

---

## TL;DR of where things stand
1. Original **black screen after login is FIXED** — cause was a missing `libnvidia-gl-595`
   (OpenGL/EGL libs) after the driver moved to 595. Installing it restored Hyprland rendering.
2. During cleanup, an over-aggressive `apt autoremove --purge` removed **205 packages**
   (nvidia userspace + KDE Plasma + some CLI tools). **RECOVERY COMMAND is below.**

---

## Root cause of the black screen (confirmed)
Driver upgraded to **595**, but matching userspace GL lib **`libnvidia-gl-595`** was missing.
Hyprland launched but had no working GL/EGL → black. SDDM (on X) still showed fine.
Fix that worked: `sudo apt install libnvidia-gl-595`. `modeset=1` was always correct.

## What went wrong during cleanup (the 205-package cascade)
- At **17:30**, `apt install libnvidia-egl-gbm1` had silently removed the **`nvidia-driver-595-open`
  metapackage** (the anchor for all nvidia userspace libs).
- With that anchor gone, all `nvidia-*` userspace libs + a pile of KDE packages were orphaned.
- The cleanup command `sudo apt-get autoremove --purge -y` then swept all 205 orphans, including:
  `nvidia-utils-595` (nvidia-smi), `xserver-xorg-video-nvidia-595`, `libnvidia-cfg1-595`,
  `libnvidia-decode/encode/fbc1/extra-595`, `nvidia-compute-utils-595`, `nvidia-settings`,
  `nvidia-prime`, the whole KDE Plasma stack, `ripgrep`, `fd-find`, `vulkan-tools`, `smartmontools`.
- SURVIVED (critical): `libnvidia-gl-595`, `libnvidia-common-595`, `libnvidia-compute-595`,
  the kernel module `linux-modules-nvidia-595-open-6.17.0-35-generic` (modinfo = 595.71.05).

## RECOVERY — reinstall everything autoremove purged (re-anchors the driver)
The exact list came from `/var/log/apt/history.log` (autoremove transaction 2026-07-11 18:14:38).
```
sudo apt-get install nvidia-driver-595-open <the 205 purged packages>
```
Rebuild the list any time with:
```
awk '/^Start-Date: 2026-07-11  18:14:38/{f=1} f&&/^Purge:/{sub(/^Purge: /,""); print; exit}' \
  /var/log/apt/history.log | sed 's/([^)]*)//g; s/,//g' | tr ' ' '\n' | sed '/^$/d' | sort -u
```
Review the apt plan: expect ~205 installs, **0 removals**. If it wants to REMOVE
`libnvidia-gl-595` or pull in `libnvidia-egl-gbm1`, stop — that's a conflict to resolve first.

## Cleanup that WAS good and should stay
- Purged half-configured `libnvidia-compute-550` (`ic` state) + old 550/580 kmod leftovers. Fine.
- Consolidated modprobe files to two:
  - `/etc/modprobe.d/nvidia-graphics-drivers-kms.conf` (driver-generated): `modeset=1` +
    `NVreg_PreserveVideoMemoryAllocations=1` + `NVreg_TemporaryFilePath=/var`
  - `/etc/modprobe.d/nvidia-hypr.conf`: `options nvidia_drm fbdev=1`
  - (deleted the redundant manual `/etc/modprobe.d/nvidia.conf`)
- `sudo update-initramfs -u` was run. Re-run it after any further modprobe change.

---

## IF BLACK SCREEN RETURNS AFTER REBOOT — diagnostics
Get a console first: **Ctrl+Alt+F3**, log in.

1. Driver loaded + matches kernel?
   ```
   nvidia-smi                                                  # needs nvidia-utils-595 reinstalled
   uname -r; modinfo -F version nvidia                         # expect 595.71.05
   dpkg -l | grep "linux-modules-nvidia-595-open-$(uname -r)"  # kmod for THIS kernel?
   ```
2. GL/EGL actually rendering? (the original culprit)
   ```
   eglinfo 2>/dev/null | grep -iE "EGL vendor|renderer" | head
   dpkg -l | grep libnvidia-gl-595       # MUST be ii  → else: sudo apt install libnvidia-gl-595
   ```
3. Hyprland errors:
   ```
   pgrep -a Hyprland
   journalctl -b 0 --no-pager | grep -iE "hyprland|EGL|GBM|drm|no monitors|render|fail" | tail -40
   ```
4. Modeset on?
   ```
   cat /sys/module/nvidia_drm/parameters/modeset   # want Y
   cat /proc/cmdline                               # nvidia-drm.modeset=1 present
   ```
5. Launch Hyprland manually from TTY to see live errors:
   ```
   Hyprland 2>&1 | tee ~/hypr-debug.log
   ```

### Recovery levers
- Boot previous kernel: GRUB > Advanced options for Ubuntu.
- Reinstall driver stack: `sudo apt install --reinstall nvidia-driver-595-open libnvidia-gl-595`
- Rebuild initramfs after modprobe changes: `sudo update-initramfs -u`
- NVIDIA+Wayland env vars if needed (Hyprland env): `LIBVA_DRIVER_NAME=nvidia`,
  `GBM_BACKEND=nvidia-drm`, `__GLX_VENDOR_LIBRARY_NAME=nvidia`, `NVD_BACKEND=direct`

### Unrelated cosmetic issue
swaync logged missing `~/.config/waybar/wallust/colors-waybar.css` (wallust-generated theme file).
Harmless; only affects notification-center colors.

## Lesson for next time
Never chain `autoremove --purge -y` blindly after purging driver packages. Run
`apt autoremove` WITHOUT `-y` first and read the plan, or scope it to named packages.

content.text:
Good question — most of the 205 were KDE Plasma internals and libraries, but here are the **actual standalone tools/apps** you lost (the ones you'd actually notice). All of these come back with the second reinstall command.

**Command-line tools:**
- `ripgrep` (`rg`) — fast grep
- `fd-find` (`fd`) — fast find
- `bup` — deduplicating backup
- `par2` — parity/repair archives
- `cryfs` — encrypted filesystem
- `smartmontools` (`smartctl`) — disk SMART health
- `vulkan-tools` (`vulkaninfo`, `vkcube`) — Vulkan diagnostics
- `wayland-utils` (`wayland-info`)
- `clinfo` — OpenCL info
- `aha` — ANSI-to-HTML converter

**NVIDIA tools** — *already restored by your first command:*
- `nvidia-settings`, `nvidia-prime`, `nvidia-utils-595` (that's `nvidia-smi`)

**GUI apps (KDE):**
- `kate` / `kwrite` — text editors
- `kfind` — file search
- `partitionmanager` — partition editor
- `plasma-discover` — software center
- `kup-backup` — backup GUI
- `kmenuedit`

**Everything else (~170 packages)** was KDE Plasma desktop machinery — `plasma-*`, `kde-*`, KDE Frameworks libs (`libkf5*`), Breeze themes, QML modules — plus supporting libraries, a few fonts (`fonts-hack`, `fonts-noto-*`), and Python modules (`python3-psutil`, `python3-pydantic`, etc.).

One thing worth deciding: **do you actually use the KDE Plasma desktop, or just Hyprland?** If you only ever log into Hyprland, you could skip restoring the bulk of the `plasma-*`/`kde-*` stack and just reinstall the standalone tools above. Want me to build a **tools-only** reinstall command instead of the full 185-package restore?

Perfect — then skip the whole KDE Plasma stack. Here's a **tools-only** command with just the desktop-agnostic utilities, no `plasma-*`/`kde-*`/`libkf5*` machinery:

```
! sudo apt-get install ripgrep fd-find bup par2 cryfs smartmontools vulkan-tools wayland-utils clinfo aha fonts-hack fonts-noto-hinted fonts-noto-ui-core fonts-noto-unhinted
```

What's in there and why:
- **`ripgrep` (`rg`), `fd-find` (`fd`)** — your fast search tools
- **`vulkan-tools`, `wayland-utils`** — genuinely handy for debugging Hyprland/NVIDIA (`vulkaninfo`, `wayland-info`)
- **`smartmontools`** — disk health (`smartctl`)
- **`bup`, `par2`, `cryfs`, `clinfo`, `aha`** — your backup/OpenCL/misc utilities
- **`fonts-hack` + `fonts-noto-*`** — monospace + wide glyph/emoji coverage (useful for waybar icons)

These are all CLI/DE-agnostic, so apt won't drag KDE back in. Expect a small install, **0 removals**.

**I intentionally left out** the KDE GUI apps (`kate`, `kwrite`, `kfind`, `partitionmanager`, `plasma-discover`, `kup-backup`) — each pulls in dozens of KDE Frameworks libs you don't need on Hyprland. If you specifically want one (e.g. `kate` as a GUI editor), say so and I'll add it, but know it brings ~40+ KDE lib packages with it.

Two quick checks before you reboot:
1. **Did the first command (`nvidia-driver-595-open`, 20 packages) finish?** That's the critical one — confirm it completed with `y`.
2. Run the tools command above.

Paste both results and I'll do a final verify (nvidia stack + rendering) so you can reboot with confidence.

## TL;DR of where things stand  — RECOVERED (verified 2026-07-11, pre-reboot)
1. Original **black screen after login is FIXED** — cause was a missing `libnvidia-gl-595`
   (OpenGL/EGL libs) after the driver moved to 595. Installing it restored Hyprland rendering.
2. During cleanup, an over-aggressive `apt autoremove --purge` removed **205 packages**
   (nvidia userspace + KDE Plasma + some CLI tools).

   + a tools-only set (ripgrep, fd-find, vulkan-tools, wayland-utils, smartmontools, etc.).

- `nvidia-smi` → RTX 3060, driver 595.71.05. All 595 userspace pkgs `ii`.
- Kernel module `595.71.05` matches running kernel `6.17.0-35-generic`.
- modprobe: `modeset=1` (generated file) + `fbdev=1` (nvidia-hypr.conf). No broken dpkg state.
- **Before reboot:** ran `sudo update-initramfs -u` as final belt-and-suspenders.

# NVIDIA Black-Screen Fix + Recovery — Handoff Notes

**Machine:** KrubicsLaptop (Ubuntu 24.04, GRUB, kernel 6.17.0-35-generic)
**GPU:** NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 Laptop + Intel UHD iGPU (Optimus/PRIME)
**Compositor:** Hyprland (Wayland) · DM: SDDM · Also had KDE Plasma installed
**Date:** 2026-07-11

---

## TL;DR of where things stand
1. Original **black screen after login is FIXED** — cause was a missing `libnvidia-gl-595`
   (OpenGL/EGL libs) after the driver moved to 595. Installing it restored Hyprland rendering.
2. During cleanup, an over-aggressive `apt autoremove --purge` removed **205 packages**
   (nvidia userspace + KDE Plasma + some CLI tools). **RECOVERY COMMAND is below.**

---

## Root cause of the black screen (confirmed)
Driver upgraded to **595**, but matching userspace GL lib **`libnvidia-gl-595`** was missing.
Hyprland launched but had no working GL/EGL → black. SDDM (on X) still showed fine.
Fix that worked: `sudo apt install libnvidia-gl-595`. `modeset=1` was always correct.

## What went wrong during cleanup (the 205-package cascade)
- At **17:30**, `apt install libnvidia-egl-gbm1` had silently removed the **`nvidia-driver-595-open`
  metapackage** (the anchor for all nvidia userspace libs).
- With that anchor gone, all `nvidia-*` userspace libs + a pile of KDE packages were orphaned.
- The cleanup command `sudo apt-get autoremove --purge -y` then swept all 205 orphans, including:
  `nvidia-utils-595` (nvidia-smi), `xserver-xorg-video-nvidia-595`, `libnvidia-cfg1-595`,
  `libnvidia-decode/encode/fbc1/extra-595`, `nvidia-compute-utils-595`, `nvidia-settings`,
  `nvidia-prime`, the whole KDE Plasma stack, `ripgrep`, `fd-find`, `vulkan-tools`, `smartmontools`.
- SURVIVED (critical): `libnvidia-gl-595`, `libnvidia-common-595`, `libnvidia-compute-595`,
  the kernel module `linux-modules-nvidia-595-open-6.17.0-35-generic` (modinfo = 595.71.05).

## RECOVERY — reinstall everything autoremove purged (re-anchors the driver)
The exact list came from `/var/log/apt/history.log` (autoremove transaction 2026-07-11 18:14:38).
```
sudo apt-get install nvidia-driver-595-open <the 205 purged packages>
```
Rebuild the list any time with:
```
awk '/^Start-Date: 2026-07-11  18:14:38/{f=1} f&&/^Purge:/{sub(/^Purge: /,""); print; exit}' \
  /var/log/apt/history.log | sed 's/([^)]*)//g; s/,//g' | tr ' ' '\n' | sed '/^$/d' | sort -u
```
Review the apt plan: expect ~205 installs, **0 removals**. If it wants to REMOVE
`libnvidia-gl-595` or pull in `libnvidia-egl-gbm1`, stop — that's a conflict to resolve first.

## Cleanup that WAS good and should stay
- Purged half-configured `libnvidia-compute-550` (`ic` state) + old 550/580 kmod leftovers. Fine.
- Consolidated modprobe files to two:
  - `/etc/modprobe.d/nvidia-graphics-drivers-kms.conf` (driver-generated): `modeset=1` +
    `NVreg_PreserveVideoMemoryAllocations=1` + `NVreg_TemporaryFilePath=/var`
  - `/etc/modprobe.d/nvidia-hypr.conf`: `options nvidia_drm fbdev=1`
  - (deleted the redundant manual `/etc/modprobe.d/nvidia.conf`)
- `sudo update-initramfs -u` was run. Re-run it after any further modprobe change.

---

## IF BLACK SCREEN RETURNS AFTER REBOOT — diagnostics
Get a console first: **Ctrl+Alt+F3**, log in.

1. Driver loaded + matches kernel?
   ```
   nvidia-smi                                                  # needs nvidia-utils-595 reinstalled
   uname -r; modinfo -F version nvidia                         # expect 595.71.05
   dpkg -l | grep "linux-modules-nvidia-595-open-$(uname -r)"  # kmod for THIS kernel?
   ```
2. GL/EGL actually rendering? (the original culprit)
   ```
   eglinfo 2>/dev/null | grep -iE "EGL vendor|renderer" | head
   dpkg -l | grep libnvidia-gl-595       # MUST be ii  → else: sudo apt install libnvidia-gl-595
   ```
3. Hyprland errors:
   ```
   pgrep -a Hyprland
   journalctl -b 0 --no-pager | grep -iE "hyprland|EGL|GBM|drm|no monitors|render|fail" | tail -40
   ```
4. Modeset on?
   ```
   cat /sys/module/nvidia_drm/parameters/modeset   # want Y
   cat /proc/cmdline                               # nvidia-drm.modeset=1 present
   ```
5. Launch Hyprland manually from TTY to see live errors:
   ```
   Hyprland 2>&1 | tee ~/hypr-debug.log
   ```

### Recovery levers
- Boot previous kernel: GRUB > Advanced options for Ubuntu.
- Reinstall driver stack: `sudo apt install --reinstall nvidia-driver-595-open libnvidia-gl-595`
- Rebuild initramfs after modprobe changes: `sudo update-initramfs -u`
- NVIDIA+Wayland env vars if needed (Hyprland env): `LIBVA_DRIVER_NAME=nvidia`,
  `GBM_BACKEND=nvidia-drm`, `__GLX_VENDOR_LIBRARY_NAME=nvidia`, `NVD_BACKEND=direct`

### Unrelated cosmetic issue
swaync logged missing `~/.config/waybar/wallust/colors-waybar.css` (wallust-generated theme file).
Harmless; only affects notification-center colors.

## Lesson for next time
Never chain `autoremove --purge -y` blindly after purging driver packages. Run
`apt autoremove` WITHOUT `-y` first and read the plan, or scope it to named packages.

**Compositor:** Hyprland (Wayland) · DM: SDDM · Also had KDE Plasma installed
**Date:** 2026-07-11

---

## TL;DR of where things stand
1. Original **black screen after login is FIXED** — cause was a missing `libnvidia-gl-595`
   (OpenGL/EGL libs) after the driver moved to 595. Installing it restored Hyprland rendering.
2. During cleanup, an over-aggressive `apt autoremove --purge` removed **205 packages**
   (nvidia userspace + KDE Plasma + some CLI tools). **RECOVERY COMMAND is below.**

---

## Root cause of the black screen (confirmed)
Driver upgraded to **595**, but matching userspace GL lib **`libnvidia-gl-595`** was missing.
Hyprland launched but had no working GL/EGL → black. SDDM (on X) still showed fine.
Fix that worked: `sudo apt install libnvidia-gl-595`. `modeset=1` was always correct.

## What went wrong during cleanup (the 205-package cascade)
- At **17:30**, `apt install libnvidia-egl-gbm1` had silently removed the **`nvidia-driver-595-open`
  metapackage** (the anchor for all nvidia userspace libs).
- With that anchor gone, all `nvidia-*` userspace libs + a pile of KDE packages were orphaned.
- The cleanup command `sudo apt-get autoremove --purge -y` then swept all 205 orphans, including:
  `nvidia-utils-595` (nvidia-smi), `xserver-xorg-video-nvidia-595`, `libnvidia-cfg1-595`,
  `libnvidia-decode/encode/fbc1/extra-595`, `nvidia-compute-utils-595`, `nvidia-settings`,
  `nvidia-prime`, the whole KDE Plasma stack, `ripgrep`, `fd-find`, `vulkan-tools`, `smartmontools`.

  the kernel module `linux-modules-nvidia-595-open-6.17.0-35-generic` (modinfo = 595.71.05).

- Purged half-configured `libnvidia-compute-550` (`ic` state) + old 550/580 kmod leftovers. Fine.
- Consolidated modprobe files to two:

    `NVreg_PreserveVideoMemoryAllocations=1` + `NVreg_TemporaryFilePath=/var`
  - `/etc/modprobe.d/nvidia-hypr.conf`: `options nvidia_drm fbdev=1`
  - (deleted the redundant manual `/etc/modprobe.d/nvidia.conf`)

Harmless; only affects notification-center colors.

2. During cleanup, an over-aggressive `apt autoremove --purge` removed **205 packages**
   (nvidia userspace + KDE Plasma + some CLI tools). **RECOVERY COMMAND is below.**

---

## Root cause of the black screen (confirmed)
Driver upgraded to **595**, but matching userspace GL lib **`libnvidia-gl-595`** was missing.
Hyprland launched but had no working GL/EGL → black. SDDM (on X) still showed fine.
Fix that worked: `sudo apt install libnvidia-gl-595`. `modeset=1` was always correct.

## What went wrong during cleanup (the 205-package cascade)
- At **17:30**, `apt install libnvidia-egl-gbm1` had silently removed the **`nvidia-driver-595-open`
  metapackage** (the anchor for all nvidia userspace libs).
- With that anchor gone, all `nvidia-*` userspace libs + a pile of KDE packages were orphaned.
- The cleanup command `sudo apt-get autoremove --purge -y` then swept all 205 orphans, including:
  `nvidia-utils-595` (nvidia-smi), `xserver-xorg-video-nvidia-595`, `libnvidia-cfg1-595`,
  `libnvidia-decode/encode/fbc1/extra-595`, `nvidia-compute-utils-595`, `nvidia-settings`,
  `nvidia-prime`, the whole KDE Plasma stack, `ripgrep`, `fd-find`, `vulkan-tools`, `smartmontools`.
- SURVIVED (critical): `libnvidia-gl-595`, `libnvidia-common-595`, `libnvidia-compute-595`,
  the kernel module `linux-modules-nvidia-595-open-6.17.0-35-generic` (modinfo = 595.71.05).

## RECOVERY — reinstall everything autoremove purged (re-anchors the driver)
The exact list came from `/var/log/apt/history.log` (autoremove transaction 2026-07-11 18:14:38).
```
sudo apt-get install nvidia-driver-595-open <the 205 purged packages>
```
Rebuild the list any time with:
```
awk '/^Start-Date: 2026-07-11  18:14:38/{f=1} f&&/^Purge:/{sub(/^Purge: /,""); print; exit}' \
  /var/log/apt/history.log | sed 's/([^)]*)//g; s/,//g' | tr ' ' '\n' | sed '/^$/d' | sort -u
```
Review the apt plan: expect ~205 installs, **0 removals**. If it wants to REMOVE
`libnvidia-gl-595` or pull in `libnvidia-egl-gbm1`, stop — that's a conflict to resolve first.

## Cleanup that WAS good and should stay
- Purged half-configured `libnvidia-compute-550` (`ic` state) + old 550/580 kmod leftovers. Fine.
- Consolidated modprobe files to two:
  - `/etc/modprobe.d/nvidia-graphics-drivers-kms.conf` (driver-generated): `modeset=1` +
    `NVreg_PreserveVideoMemoryAllocations=1` + `NVreg_TemporaryFilePath=/var`
  - `/etc/modprobe.d/nvidia-hypr.conf`: `options nvidia_drm fbdev=1`
  - (deleted the redundant manual `/etc/modprobe.d/nvidia.conf`)
- `sudo update-initramfs -u` was run. Re-run it after any further modprobe change.

---

## IF BLACK SCREEN RETURNS AFTER REBOOT — diagnostics
Get a console first: **Ctrl+Alt+F3**, log in.

1. Driver loaded + matches kernel?
   ```
   nvidia-smi                                                  # needs nvidia-utils-595 reinstalled
   uname -r; modinfo -F version nvidia                         # expect 595.71.05
   dpkg -l | grep "linux-modules-nvidia-595-open-$(uname -r)"  # kmod for THIS kernel?
   ```
2. GL/EGL actually rendering? (the original culprit)
   ```
   eglinfo 2>/dev/null | grep -iE "EGL vendor|renderer" | head
   dpkg -l | grep libnvidia-gl-595       # MUST be ii  → else: sudo apt install libnvidia-gl-595
   ```
3. Hyprland errors:
   ```
   pgrep -a Hyprland
   journalctl -b 0 --no-pager | grep -iE "hyprland|EGL|GBM|drm|no monitors|render|fail" | tail -40
   ```
4. Modeset on?
   ```
   cat /sys/module/nvidia_drm/parameters/modeset   # want Y
   cat /proc/cmdline                               # nvidia-drm.modeset=1 present
   ```
5. Launch Hyprland manually from TTY to see live errors:
   ```
   Hyprland 2>&1 | tee ~/hypr-debug.log
   ```

### Recovery levers
- Boot previous kernel: GRUB > Advanced options for Ubuntu.
- Reinstall driver stack: `sudo apt install --reinstall nvidia-driver-595-open libnvidia-gl-595`
- Rebuild initramfs after modprobe changes: `sudo update-initramfs -u`
- NVIDIA+Wayland env vars if needed (Hyprland env): `LIBVA_DRIVER_NAME=nvidia`,
  `GBM_BACKEND=nvidia-drm`, `__GLX_VENDOR_LIBRARY_NAME=nvidia`, `NVD_BACKEND=direct`

### Unrelated cosmetic issue
swaync logged missing `~/.config/waybar/wallust/colors-waybar.css` (wallust-generated theme file).
Harmless; only affects notification-center colors.

## Lesson for next time
Never chain `autoremove --purge -y` blindly after purging driver packages. Run
`apt autoremove` WITHOUT `-y` first and read the plan, or scope it to named packages.
